name: ARES Gale Crater elevation window (MOLA 463 m)
format: Raw 16-bit signed integers, little-endian, row-major, first row is the NORTH edge, first column is the WEST edge. Value -32768 means no data.

bounds.note: Outer pixel edges (assuming the file's pixel convention below).

projection: Simple cylindrical, centre longitude 0 (from the file name and tie point), longitude positive east.

sphereRadius_m.note: ARES distance maths uses 3389500 m, a difference of about 0.2%.

geoKeys.rasterTypeNote: 1 = PixelIsArea, 2 = PixelIsPoint. If PixelIsArea, positions are good to about one pixel (463 m).
geoKeys.text: Mars2000_ECylindrical_clon0|GCS Name = GCS_Mars_2000_Sphere|Datum = Mars_2000_(Sphere)|Ellipsoid = Mars_2000_Sphere|Primem = Reference_Meridian||

heightReference: Not stated in the file. Do not call these heights above sea level.

stats.note: Bradbury check is a rough sanity test only; it is not an independent verification.

source.how: This S3 link was given by a USGS staff member on the OpenPlanetary forum. It is not an official USGS product page, and it could change or disappear.
source.product: MOLA 128 pixel/degree DEM merged with 64 pixel/degree (file name), 463 m per pixel
source.licence: CC0 according to the USGS Astropedia listing (not re-checked by this tool)

limitations: 463 m per pixel cannot show features smaller than several hundred metres, including boxwork ridges (about 1 to 2 m tall).
Not suitable for obstacle detection or any local safety assessment.
MOLA gaps between laser tracks are interpolated in this product (reported in project research; not re-checked here).
evidenceNote: Elevation values come from the file unchanged. Only cropping to this window was done by ARES.
